newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek customs officials' strike on 17-19 December.
newsitem.headline: Greek customs officials' strike on 17-19 December.

text.p: Greek customs officers said they would join tax, accounting and other finance ministry officials in a three-day strike starting on December 17.
A statement by the customs officials union said that their action would hit all Greek borders, ports and airports.
The pre-Christmas strike will further exacerbate travellers and commercial transport in Greece, which is already paralyzed by a 13-day farmers' road and rail blockade.
The union said its members were striking to protest against a fall in income, the liquidation of subsidiary insurance funds and the abolition of long-established customs institutions.
They are also seeking the hiring of new personnel and the computerisation of their service to be better equipped to combat illegal acitivities such as tax evation and smuggling.

Greece is already under pressure from a series of strikes to protest against the socialist government's 1997 budget. The two largest labour confederations have called a one-day strike for December 17.
